headline: US Crude Inventories Fall by 900,000 Barrels on Sustained Demand
summary: U.S. crude oil inventories decreased by 900,000 barrels for the week ending October 30, driven by steady demand. Commercial stockpiles fell to 409.8 million barrels, standing 4% below the five-year seasonal average.
why: The Energy Information Administration (EIA) weekly inventory report is a key indicator of supply and demand dynamics in the U.S. petroleum market, closely watched by energy traders.

impacts.name: WTI Crude Oil
impacts.why: A larger-than-expected decline in U.S. crude inventories typically signals stronger demand and tighter supply, supporting oil prices.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A reduction in commercial crude stockpiles amid steady demand points to tighter physical market conditions, which can exert upward pressure on oil prices.
